subject: Request: provisional credits while PO routes (Orion Health evaluation)

Subject: Eval access and PO routing delay

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the demo last week. The engineering team is progressing but procurement has bumped our PO to the legal queue (apparently a new data-processing clause). Our procurement lead estimates 10–12 business days to issue a PO.

We really want to keep testing model latencies against our integration. Would Redwood be willing to provision temporary credits (or a short trial extension) while the PO routes? A two-week buffer would let us finish the integration and produce a short internal evaluation for legal.

If you need a procurement contact or any paperwork to justify credits internally, I can share details — our procurement alias is procurement@orionhealth.com and the procurement lead is Priya Mehta.

Appreciate any help here.

—Samir
Senior Engineering Manager, Orion Health

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the heads up and for outlining the timeline. Happy to help keep the evaluation live while procurement finishes. Two options that usually work:

- Short trial extension (14 days) on the current eval tenant, or
- Provisional credits applied to your account to cover the next 2 weeks of usage (consumed against the first invoice once PO is in).

Rishi — can you confirm the amount we typically offer for a 2-week keep-alive for an integration like this? Dev, I’ll loop you in if we need to adjust quotas on the eval instance.

Samir, if procurement needs a short pro forma or a statement of intent from Redwood, we can produce a one-page credit note and an internal approval thread. Do you want us to send that to Priya or the procurement alias?

Best,
Naomi

Looping in sales ops details.

Naomi — for a standard two-week keep-alive we typically provision a provisional credit equal to $3,000 (applies to hosted usage and expires if a PO isn't received within 30 days). If Orion prefers a straight extension of the trial window on the tenant (no credit exchange), we can do that too — same expiry policy.

Samir — to expedite internal approvals we can provide:
- A short credit note (one-page PDF) referencing Orion Health and deal id ORN-2026-082
- A footprint estimate (we recommend reserving up to 200k tokens for two weeks)

If procurement wants a pro forma invoice or DocuSign acknowledgement we can provide a provisional agreement. Linking the HubSpot record here for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/contact/67890.

Let me know which route you prefer and who to send the paperwork to.

Thanks,

Thanks Rishi — that sounds reasonable. Procurement prefers a short credit note (PDF) addressed to Orion Health and a token estimate. They want the credit to be explicitly labeled as provisional and will treat it as a pre-credit against the upcoming PO.

I've copied Priya Mehta (procurement lead) on the procurement alias; Priya, could you confirm if procurement@orionhealth.com is sufficient or if you need the credit note routed to a different address (vendor onboarding team)?

Given our internal timelines, could Redwood provision a 14-calendar-day credit window starting as soon as the credit note is signed/issued? That should give us time to finish technical validation and get legal sign-off on the PO.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we want to avoid redoing any integration work.

—Samir

- Window: 14 calendar days from issuance (credits expire 2026-06-18T15:06:00-04:00)
